title: Canonical residue trace and cup-product pairing
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $C/k$ be a smooth projective curve [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve], with generic point $\eta$ and function field $K=\mathcal O_{C,\eta}$ [def-sc-function-field]. Give $K$ the canonical $k$-algebra structure $k\to\Gamma(C,\mathcal O_C)\to\mathcal O_{C,\eta}$ induced by the structure morphism and the germ map. Write $\omega=\Omega^1_{C/k}$ [def-sc-kahler-differentials]. Define the residue trace $t_C:H^1(C,\omega)\to k$ [def-pc-euler-characteristic] by sending an adelic principal-parts representative $(\alpha_x)_{x\text{ closed}}$ to $\sum_x\operatorname{res}_x(\alpha_x)$, where $\operatorname{res}_x$ is Tate's local residue on rational differentials, vanishing on differentials regular at $x$; the residue theorem makes this independent of the representative. For an $\mathcal O_C$-module $\mathcal F$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with sheaf dual $\mathcal F^\vee=\mathcal Hom(\mathcal F,\mathcal O_C)$ [def-sc-invertible-module] and sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], define the trace cup-pairing map $H^0(C,\mathcal F^\vee\otimes\omega)\to H^1(C,\mathcal F)^\vee$ by $b\mapsto(a\mapsto t_C(H^1(\operatorname{ev})(a\mathbin\cup b)))$, where $\operatorname{ev}:\mathcal F\otimes(\mathcal F^\vee\otimes\omega)\to\omega$ sends $s\otimes(\varphi\otimes w)$ to $\varphi(s)w$. This definition asserts no perfectness.
